description.narrative: The Project Development Objective (PDO) is to enhance SODECA's and ENERCA's operational performance and to increase access to improved water supply and electricity in Bangui and selected towns.

The development objective of the Water and Electricity Upgrading Project for Central African Republic is to enhance SODECA's and ENERCA's operational performance and to increase access to improved water supply and electricity in Bangui and selected towns. There are four project components. (1) Water supply infrastructure; (2) Energy infrastructure; (3) Technical Support to Water and Energy Sectors; and (4) Contingent Emergency Response. The first component will carry out improvements of the water supply infrastructure in Bangui, Bambari and Berberati and thus help achieve the PDO targets of improving access and improving operational efficiency. The second component will enhance continuity of power supply, extend access and reduce losses in Bangui, and restore generating capacity and the distribution network in the secondary towns of Bambari and Berberati. The third component will support technical assistance to the utilities SODECA and ENERCA to improve their operational performance in line with the PDO, as well as activities aimed at better long-term sector planning of the umbrella MDEWR, and support to the project implementation unit (PIU) to ensure an efficient project implementation and compliance with World Bank procedures. The fourth component is to improve the Government's ability to respond effectively in the event of an emergency, following the procedures governed by Paragraph 13 (disaster prevention and preparedness) of the World Bank IPF Policy.

condition.narrative: Schedule 2, Section I.A.2.a.The Recipient shall, not later than one (1) month after the Effective Date, conclude, and throughoutProject implementation adopt an inter-ministerial decree between MDEWR and MTCA for the purposes of ensuring adequate coordinationbetween the relevant ministries relative to the PIU.

Schedule 2, Section I.A.2.b. The Recipient shall, not later than one (1) month after the Effective Date, conclude, and throughoutProject implementation maintain a Memorandum of Understanding between the PIU, SODECA and ENERCA for the purposes of ensuringtechnical support for the Project from the two utilities and to define their roles and responsibilities relative to the PIU.

Schedule 2, Section I.A.3.a. The Recipient shall, within one (1) month of the Effective Date, establish, and at all times duringProject implementation maintain, the Steering Committee (“SC”) with composition and mandate acceptable to the Association.

Schedule 2, Section I.A.4.d. The PIU shall, no later than two (2) months after the Effective Date, recruit and thereafter retain afinancial management specialist with terms of reference, qualifications, and experience satisfactory to the Association.
Schedule 2, Section I.A.4.e. The PIU shall, no later than two (2) months after the Effective Date, have customized accountingsoftware installed.
Schedule 2, Section I.C.2. The Recipient shall, no later than one (1) month after the Effective Date, furnish the annual work planand budget for the Project for the first year of implementation.

Schedule 2, Section I.D.3.a. The Recipient shall ensure that for each activity under the Project of a type for which the ESAPprovides that an ESMP or ESIA must be prepared that such ESMP or ESIA shall, within six (6) months of the Effective Date, beprepared, in form and substance satisfactory to the Association.

Schedule 2, Section I.D.4.a. The Recipient shall ensure that for each activity of a type for which the ESAP provides that a RAPmust be prepared that such RAP shall, within six (6) months of the Effective Date, be prepared, in form and substance satisfactoryto the Association (including, without limitation to the above, the provision of funds for resettlement compensation when and ifrequired under said RAP).

Schedule 2, Section I.D.5. The Recipient shall, no later than six (6) months after the Effective Date, ensure that the diagnosticstudy on dam safety has been completed, in accordance with terms of reference satisfactory to the Association.

Schedule 2, Section I.E. The Recipient shall, no later than six (6) months after the Effective Date, appoint an external auditorwith terms of reference, qualifications and experience satisfactory to the Association.

title.narrative: Water quality tests at rehabilitated utility water storage that meet required standards

comment.narrative: <p>The project envisioned to institutionalize monthly systematic E.coli and/or coliform bacteria tests at the restored water towers in Bambari and Berberati, but unfortunately this was not realized prior to project closure due to the delays in the works and capacty limitations of SODECA.</p>

title.narrative: Water production capacity constructed or rehabilitated

comment.narrative: <p>The value achieved represents a 108% achievement of the revised target. This was achieved through the installation of all planned water production infrastructure in the three cities, with the installed pumps in Bambari surpassing the specifications originally called for in the project design.</p>

title.narrative: Generation capacity of energy constructed or rehabilitated

comment.narrative: <p>The achieved value represents a 280% achievement of the target, accounting for the larger capacity of installed generation equipment at the Boali 1 hydropower plant, as well as in Bambari and Berberati. This value accounts for the 1 MW additional capacity installed at Boali, plus the 0.8 MW and 1 MW solar capacity at Bambari and Berberati respectively, although additional thermal capacity and battery storage was installed to permit system functioning when solar is not available.</p>

title.narrative: People provided with access to improved water sources

comment.narrative: <p>The value achieved represents a 56% achievement of the original target and a 70% achievement of the restructured target. Underachievement was principally related to the cancellation of works contracts in Bambari and Berberati due to lack of sufficient progress by the contractor, which prevented the construction of 53 of the planned 100 community water points post-restructuring. Meanwhile,he project actually overachieved on the number of people provided access through household connections with respect to the restructured target, as the overachievement of the target in Bangui compensated for the underachievement in Bambari.</p>

title.narrative: People provided with new or improved electricity service

comment.narrative: <p>The achieved value represents a 156% achievement of the target. This overachievement was made possible by the installation of additional household connections and meters versus the original project design (more meters installed in general, and a greater quantity of prepaid household meters versus smart meters for bulk customers).</p>

title.narrative: New piped household water connections that are resulting from the project intervention

comment.narrative: <p>The value achieved represents a 73% achievement of the original target and a 101% achievement of the restructured target. All 300 household connections planned in Berberati were successfully developed, while only 137 of the 300 planned in Bambari were developed. However, the overachievement of the target in Bangui more than compensated for the underachievement in Bambari: 2,188 household connections were installed against a restructured target of 2,000.</p>

title.narrative: Turbine alternators of Boali 1 hydropower plant refurbished

comment.narrative: <p>The value achieved represents full achievement of the target, as all planned refurbished turbine alternators were installed at the Boali 1 hydropower plant.</p>

title.narrative: Improved community water points constructed or rehabilitated under the project

comment.narrative: <p>The value achieved represents a 41% achievement of the original target and a 47% achievement of the restructured target. Underachievement was principally related to the cancellation of works contracts in Bambari and Berberati due to lack of sufficient progress by the contractor, which prevented the construction of 53 of the planned 100 community water points post-restructuring.</p>

title.narrative: Prepaid and smart electricity meters installed

comment.narrative: <p>The 5,500 installed meters represents an achievement of 106% of the target, as cost savings allowed the procurement and installation of 300 additional meters.</p>
<p>Target increase was exceeded by 60% on account of the successful installation of prepaid and smart electricity meters.</p>

title.narrative: Non-Revenue Water in the project area

comment.narrative: <p>Target reduction was exceeded by 120% on account of improvements to production and distribution systems in Bangui and Berberati, reducing technical losses.</p>
